title: grassfield.json (contract version 1)
description: User configuration of Grassfield Desktop. Unknown keys are ignored by the shell; migrations are explicit (master-prompt §5.3).

zoom.description: Screen magnification on (Hyprland cursor:zoom_factor); toggled by Super+Alt+8.

zoomLevel.description: Magnification factor while zoom is on.

history.description: How long the notification history stays on disk: a week (default), a day, or never (bodies of apps whose previews are Never are never stored).

appStyles.description: Per-app alert style (at most 200): apps listed here use alerts (stay until dismissed) or none (no banner) instead of banners. app is the sender's name.

appPreviews.description: Per-app Show previews (at most 200): the apps listed here override notifications.previews. app is the sender's name.

idleMinutes.description: Minutes without input before the session locks; 0 = never. Fail closed: only an exact 0 means never. A value below 0, or a fraction that rounds to 0 (0.4), is invalid and reads as the default 5, so no invalid number can switch the auto-lock off.

displayOffBattery.description: Minutes without input on battery before the displays turn off while the session is unlocked (macOS 27 Lock Screen: Turn display off on battery when inactive); 0 = never. Any input turns them on again; the lock follows lock.idleMinutes.

displayOffPower.description: Minutes without input on the power adapter before the displays turn off while the session is unlocked (Turn display off on power adapter when inactive); 0 = never.

requirePasswordAfterDisplayOff.description: When a display that turned off for inactivity locks the session (ADR-0040 IQ-T4 A, macOS's Require password after the display is turned off): at once (the lock is drawn just before the displays go off), after this delay with no input, or never. lock.idleMinutes stays the ceiling either way.

showUser.description: The lock screen shows the account's name and picture (Show user name and photo).

showMessage.description: The lock screen shows lock.message (Show message when locked).

message.description: The message the lock screen shows: one line of plain text of at most 200 UTF-16 code units (as the settings contract counts), without control characters (C0, C1), line or paragraph separators or bidirectional overrides and isolates.

preventSleep.description: The computer does not go to sleep by itself once the displays are off for inactivity, on battery and on the power adapter alike (macOS 27 Energy, and Battery > Options…: Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off; integrator decision 2026-11-04: macOS has no switch for battery, Grassfield does). Off: it sleeps a minute after the displays went off, only while its lock is confirmed. The displays still turn off and the session still locks as lock.* says; the only lock this key can add is the one before an automatic sleep. Default on: a Grassfield computer never went to sleep by itself before this key, and an unreadable value keeps it that way.

slowHiddenApps.description: Apps the person cannot see get less CPU and I/O (ADR-0048, Battery > Options…): on battery an app covered by the focused window for 10 s gets CPUWeight 40 and IOWeight 60, one hidden (minimized, hidden, on another Desktop) for 30 s 20 and 30. Nothing is limited on the power adapter (and so never on a computer without a battery): plugging in lifts everything. The app in front, apps playing or recording, holding an alarm or still working are never limited; everything is lifted at once when the person looks for an app (overview, app switcher, Dock, focus) or plugs in. Off: no limit at all.

main.description: The main display (ADR-0044): one remembered choice per set of connected displays, newest first, at most 16. `set` is the sorted identities of the displays (model|serial, else model|connector, else the connector), `main` the one of them that holds the Dock, the desktop icons and the notifications. No entry for the connected set: the newest choice whose display is connected, else the built-in panel, else the first display.

autoHide.description: Automatically hide and show the menu bar (Settings > Menu Bar): "always" hides it on the desktop and in full screen, "desktop" on the desktop only, "fullscreen" (default) in full screen only, "never" keeps it in view. A hidden bar slides in over the window when the pointer reaches the top edge. Only "fullscreen" and "never" reserve space for the bar.

showNowPlaying.description: Show the Now Playing item in the menu bar while a media player has a session (playing, or paused with a track loaded). Default true.

showSearch.description: Show the Search item (magnifier) in the menu bar. Default true.

showWifi.description: Show the network item (Wi-Fi or wired status) in the menu bar (Settings > Menu Bar). Default true.

showSound.description: Show the Sound (volume) item in the menu bar. Default true.

showBattery.description: Show the Battery item in the menu bar (a machine without a battery never shows it). Default true.

showBatteryPercentage.description: Show the charge percentage beside the battery glyph. Default true.

showFocus.description: Show the Focus (Do Not Disturb) item in the menu bar while it is on. Default true.

clockDate.description: Date (day and month) in the menu bar clock: "auto" (When Space Allows, default) drops it when the status items would not fit, "always" keeps it, "never" hides it.

clockShowDayOfWeek.description: Show the day of the week in the menu bar clock. Default true.

clockHours.description: Hour format of the menu bar clock: "auto" follows the locale, "12" shows AM/PM, "24" a 24-hour time. Default auto.

clockShowAmPm.description: Show AM/PM in a 12-hour menu bar clock. Default true.

clockFlashSeparators.description: Flash the colons of the menu bar clock once a second (the clock then wakes every second). Default false.

showTrayItems.description: Show the status items of other applications (StatusNotifierItem tray icons) in the menu bar. Default true.

recentItems.description: How many recent applications and documents the Grassfield menu's Recent Items lists (0 hides Recent Items). Default 10.

clockShowSeconds.description: Show seconds in the menu bar clock (the clock then wakes every second). Default false.

accent.description: Accent colour (Settings > Appearance > Accent colour). A nested `appearance.accent` cannot exist in contract version 1, where `appearance` is a string (the same reason as the `icons` keys, ADR-0014).

color.description: "multicolor" keeps each surface's own colour, for Grassfield the Grassfield green (default); the others replace the accent of menus, selections, toggles, focus rings and the Tinted and folder colours that follow it. The highlight colour (text selection) follows the accent unless `accent.highlight` names its own.

highlight.description: Text highlight colour (Settings > Appearance > Text highlight colour, macOS 27): the colour of selected text in fields and editors, in the shell and the apps. "automatic" follows the accent (default); a name uses that accent colour whatever the accent is.

terminal.description: Terminal and developer apps (Settings > Appearance > Terminal and Developer Apps, ADR-0045 OC-11): Omarchy's theme, which its terminals, editors and developer tools follow, changed with the effective appearance. ADR-0045 names these keys `appearance.terminal*`; a nested `appearance` object cannot exist in contract version 1, where `appearance` is a string (the same reason as `accent`).

matchAppearance.description: Match Appearance: when the effective appearance changes (Light, Dark, Auto at its hours) and once at login, the shell runs `grassfield-terminal-theme light|dark`, which applies `lightTheme` or `darkTheme` with Omarchy's `omarchy-theme-set`. The Omarchy session shares that theme and its wallpaper. Default false.

lightTheme.description: The Omarchy theme of the light appearance, as `omarchy-theme-list` names it ("Catppuccin Latte"). A theme that is no longer installed is left alone (omarchy-theme-set refuses it). Default "Catppuccin Latte" (a light theme of Omarchy 4.0.6).

darkTheme.description: The Omarchy theme of the dark appearance, as `omarchy-theme-list` names it. Default "Tokyo Night" (Omarchy's own default theme).

shortcutStyle.description: How menus show keyboard shortcuts: "mac" with the macOS symbols (⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘, ⌘ for Super), "pc" as text (Ctrl+Shift+Q). "automatic" (default) picks mac on Apple hardware (firmware vendor "Apple Inc.") or with an Apple keyboard attached, pc otherwise (owner decision 2026-10-26, ADR-0024).

showInputMenu.description: Show the Input menu (the input source in use, FR or US) in the menu bar (Settings > Keyboard > Input Sources). The menu only exists with two input sources or more, as on macOS, where it is on by default from two. Default true.

dictation.description: Dictation (Settings > Keyboard > Dictation, ADR-0045 OC-5): Ctrl-Super-X starts and stops Omarchy's voxtype (`voxtype record toggle`, speech recognised on this computer) when this is on and voxtype is installed. Read by config/hypr/grassfield/bindings.lua when the key is pressed. Default false.

region.description: Formats of dates, times and numbers (Settings > General > Language & Region). The language itself is Omarchy's (omarchy-language).

formats.description: The locale whose formats the shell uses for dates, times and numbers ("fr_CH": Swiss French). "auto" (default) follows the language. The language's words stay; only the formats change.

firstDayOfWeek.description: The first day of the week in the calendars. "auto" (default) follows the formats.

textInImages.description: Select Text in Images (Settings > General > Language & Region; macOS: Live Text; ADR-0045 OC-2): Preview and Glance read the text and the QR codes of a still image with tesseract and zbarimg when they are installed, so that its words can be selected and copied and a QR code's link opened. Read in the background from the file, never stored. Default true.

icons.description: Icon appearance of Grassfield surfaces (ADR-0014): app and file icons only, never symbolic glyphs.

tint.description: "accent" follows the accent colour, else a #rrggbb colour used by the tinted mode.

folderColor.description: Colour of every folder icon: "theme" keeps the icon theme's own colour, "accent" follows the accent colour, else a #rrggbb colour. A folder's own colour (Customize Folder) wins.

size.description: Cursor size in pixels (the macOS slider Normal to Large). Applied live by the shell; the XCursor fallback uses the nearest of 24, 32, 48, 64, 96.

outlineColor.description: Pointer outline colour (#rrggbb). The default #ffffff is the packaged cursor theme; any other pair makes the shell regenerate the theme grassfield-cursors-custom.

fillColor.description: Pointer fill colour (#rrggbb). The default #000000 is the packaged cursor theme.

capture.description: The capture toolbar (Shift-Super-5, ADR-0045 OC-1; macOS 27's screenshot toolbar): the mode chosen last and its Options menu. The toolbar writes these keys itself; no Settings pane shows them (as macOS).

mode.description: The mode the toolbar opens in (the one chosen last): Capture Entire Screen, Capture Selected Window, Capture Selected Portion, Record Entire Screen, Record Selected Portion.

saveTo.description: Superseded by `location` (1.0.0-rc7); kept so that older files stay valid. Read only while `location` is absent: its documents, clipboard and preview stay chosen, and its desktop (the old default, which every file the shell created held, so it cannot be told from a choice) reads as `location`'s default. Nothing writes it any more.

location.description: Options > Save to (owner 2026-11-07: never the Desktop by default): `screenshots` the Screenshots folder in the Pictures folder (xdg-user-dir PICTURES; the folder named in the session's language, made on first use) for a screenshot and the Videos folder (xdg-user-dir VIDEOS) for a recording; the Desktop; the Documents folder; the clipboard only (screenshots; a recording then goes to the Videos folder); or Preview (the file is kept where `screenshots` puts it and opened in Preview). The toolbar writes it; the screenshot keys follow it too.

timer.description: Options > Timer: a countdown of 5 or 10 seconds before the capture or the recording starts.

microphone.description: Options > Microphone (recordings): none, or the default input. The desktop's own sound is never recorded (macOS).

showPointer.description: Options > Show Mouse Pointer: the pointer is drawn in screenshots and recordings.

lastSelection.description: The last frame of Capture/Record Selected Portion per display, which the toolbar opens on again (macOS): `NAME=x,y,w,h` entries joined by `;` (at most 16), the display's connector name and the frame in its own logical coordinates; a frame off its display is brought back on it, an empty value or a display without one gets a centred frame. The toolbar writes it.

showApps.description: Search shows applications (Settings > Search > Search Results: Applications).

showDocuments.description: Search shows documents found on this computer (localsearch, plocate) (Settings > Search > Search Results: Documents).

showRecents.description: Search shows recently used documents (Settings > Search > Search Results: Recent Documents).

showCalculator.description: Search shows the calculator's answer (Settings > Search > Search Results: Calculator).

showConversions.description: Search shows unit conversions (Settings > Search > Search Results: Conversions).

showSettings.description: Search shows Settings panes (Settings > Search > Search Results: Settings).

showCommands.description: Search shows system commands (Lock Screen, Sleep, Restart, Shut Down, Log Out) (Settings > Search > Search Results: System Commands).

historyResetAt.description: Milliseconds since the epoch of the last Delete Search History (Settings > Search): the shell forgets the results the user picked before it (search-usage.json). 0 = never deleted.

clipboard.description: The clipboard history in Search (ADR-0034): captured by grassfield-clipboard-helper while it is on.

enabled.description: Results from Clipboard (Settings > Search; macOS 27). Off until the user allows it (the Clipboard view's prompt). Turning it off deletes the unpinned items; pinned items stay on disk, unread.

retention.description: How long an unpinned item stays in the history: 30 minutes, 8 hours or 7 days (macOS 27's three choices). Pinned items never expire.

keepOnDisk.description: Keep clipboard history after logging out (a Grassfield addition): the unpinned items are also written to $XDG_STATE_HOME/grassfield/clipboard/history (0600). Turning it off deletes that store.

clearedAt.description: Milliseconds since the epoch of the last Clear Clipboard History (Settings > Search): the shell deletes every unpinned item when it changes. 0 = never cleared.

pinnedClearedAt.description: Milliseconds since the epoch of the last Clear Clipboard History with "Also delete pinned items": the shell deletes the pinned items too when it changes. 0 = never.

screensaver.description: Screen saver (Settings > Wallpaper > Screen Saver, ADR-0032).

idleMinutes.description: Minutes without input before the screen saver starts while the session is unlocked; 0 = never. It never delays or replaces the idle lock (lock.idleMinutes) or the display power-off.

kind.description: Which screen saver: the Grassfield artwork drifting, the wallpaper with a clock, a folder's pictures as a slideshow, a clock alone, or the moving Grassfield artwork (ADR-0040 step 9).

folder.description: The slideshow's folder: an absolute path (no control characters, at most 4096 bytes); "" = the user's Pictures folder.

sound.description: Sound effects (Settings > Sound > Sound Effects, ADR-0047 part B).

alert.description: The alert sound (the error bell of applications): one of Grassfield's own sounds, /usr/share/sounds/grassfield/stereo/grassfield-alert-<id>.wav.

alertVolume.description: Volume of the alert and the interface sounds, relative to the output's volume, on the cubic scale of the volume keys; 0 silences the alert.

effectsOutput.description: Where the alert and the interface sounds play: "" = the selected sound output device; else a PipeWire node name (used while that output is connected, the selected device otherwise).

uiEffects.description: Play user interface sound effects: Empty Trash, an item removed from the Dock, power connected, the screenshot shutter.

volumeFeedback.description: Play feedback when the volume is changed with the volume keys (once the keys rest).

store.description: Grassfield Store (its settings window, Ctrl+,; ADR-0037 a, c, SD20). The Store writes these keys itself, with these rules, as the Settings app writes its own, until the shell is the single writer (ADR-0020 decision 4).

sources.description: The optional sources (owner ST2): both off until the user turns them on.

aur.description: The AUR (ADR-0037 a, step 3b2): its search results after Return, its pages, and installs through Omarchy's terminal with the warning (spec SR16). Off: nothing is asked of aur.archlinux.org.

flathub.description: Flathub (ADR-0037 a, step 3c), offered only when flatpak is installed. Read only until step 3c.

screenshots.description: Screenshots on product pages (owner ST6), fetched when a page opens from the addresses AppStream gives.

updates.description: Software Update (Settings > General > Software Update, ADR-0033).

automaticCheck.description: Check for Grassfield and Omarchy releases in the background: 10 minutes after the session starts, then every 6 hours, never while offline or on a metered connection (ADR-0033 d.5). Opening the pane and Check Now check whatever this says; nothing is ever downloaded or installed without the user.

wallpaper.description: Wallpaper (Settings > Wallpaper, ADR-0016). Invalid values read as the defaults.

source.description: builtin = the Grassfield artwork; color = a plain colour; file = one picture; folder = a carousel of the pictures of one folder; video = a looping video (played only while the pause rules allow it); online = the daily picture of wallpaper.online.provider (off by default: it contacts the network once a day, ADR-0016 step 2).

path.description: Absolute path (no control characters, at most 4096 bytes) of the picture, folder or video; checked by the stores, not by the schema.

color.description: #rrggbb: the plain colour, and the backdrop of fit, centre and tile.

fit.description: How a picture fills the screen (a video uses fill or fit only).

interval.description: Folder only: when the picture changes (login = once, when the shell starts).

shuffle.description: Folder only: random order, no repeat until every picture was shown; false = name order.

videoOnBattery.description: Video only: keep playing on battery power.

online.description: Online source only (wallpaper.source = online). Nothing is fetched while another source is chosen.

provider.description: commons = the Wikimedia Commons Picture of the Day (commons.wikimedia.org, thumb.wikimedia.org and upload.wikimedia.org, once a day). apod = NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day (api.nasa.gov and apod.nasa.gov, once a day; copyrighted days are shown with their credit).

artwork.description: The Grassfield artwork the builtin source draws (ADR-0040 step 2): the Grassfield hills, Meadow, Field Rows or Ridgeline.

artworkVariant.description: Which variant of the artwork shows: the time of day (the Grassfield artwork only; the others read it as automatic), the appearance's (automatic), or always the light or the dark one.

moving.description: The Grassfield artwork moves (ADR-0040 IQ-W3 A, step 9): clouds drift and the light changes slowly; it pauses like a video wallpaper (locked, full screen, idle, on battery unless videoOnBattery, Reduce Motion, the Reduced profile). Off by default.

outputs.description: Per-display overrides (at most 16); omitted fields come from the top level. An override of a display that is not connected stays stored.

display.description: A display: model and serial when the serial is not empty, else the connector name.
